synopsis: The corpus recommends using simulation to select scarce physical tests and expand evidence around physical anchors, rather than promising wholesale replacement; no checked credibility framework prescribes a universal physical-test percentage [f484, f11311, f7534]. Physical tests should identify parameters, validate model fidelity, confirm boundaries and high-risk outcomes, and satisfy deterministic requirements, while simulation fills the validated domain’s interior [f6137, f7396, f7536, f4110]. Substitution should remain inside a measured, independently reviewed credibility envelope, with physical testing retained for weakly modelled conditions such as dust, soiling, vibration and heavy rain [f10467, f4972, f74]. Every documented reduction depended on years of prior investment, a narrow operating envelope, or both; Volvo CE’s reverse-only wheel-loader example covers 3–15 km/h, making the proposal to replace most physical testing within four months a substantial credibility challenge [f59, f1258, f10389]. No off-road acceptance of simulation replacing prescribed physical tests was found, and ISO 3450 requires physical brake-performance testing, but incomplete access to full standards prevents treating non-discovery as a blanket prohibition [f2103, f10431, f7544].
